purpose: shape the whole experience of a task so that users can finish it with little effort, by structuring flows, content and feedback
entry_criteria: Success measures for the tasks are defined
procedure: Describe the key tasks as flows from start to finish, including where users arrive from and what they do next.
Reduce steps and decisions: remove unneeded fields, set sensible defaults and show only what is relevant.
Organize content and navigation around the words and groupings users use, and test them with a card sort or a tree test.
Design feedback for every action and every failure, with messages that say what happened and what to do.
Test the flows with real users using prototype tasks, and measure completion, time and errors.
Revise and record the changes with the evidence that drove them.
acceptance_criteria: Key tasks have measured completion and error rates
Errors say what to do next

validation.check: check each key task has a completion rate from a test with at least five participants
read every error message and check it states cause and next step

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A booking flow of seven steps is reduced to four by defaulting known details; a test with six users shows five complete it unaided, and error text now tells the user how to correct a date.
